Thanks for connecting — excited to explore working with Redwood for lead capture at our Moscone booth (June 8–10). A few things up front:

Hi Sarah — great to meet you over email. Short answers and a proposed flow below; we can walk through on a tech call.

Supported ingest paths (onfloor):
- Webhook (JSON): recommended. Example payloads: name, email, company, phone, badge_id, source, consent_given (bool), consent_ts, capture_method.
- SFTP/CSV: hourly batches (we can auto-parse with a mapping template).
- API pull: we can poll partner endpoints if needed.

Proposed Redwood onfloor ingestion flow:
1) Scanner/form -> Redwood staging endpoint (webhook or SFTP).
2) Ingest pipeline: schema validation, prefix dedupe (badge_id + email), enrich (IP, geo), consent validation.
3) Consent fail path: records flagged and stored in restricted bucket; no push to HubSpot until consent confirmed.
4) Mapping & push: apply HubSpot field mapping, upsert as Contact with company association.
5) Audit: store per-record logs (who/when), and expose per-event export for audits.

I attached our first-pass mapping workbook (onfloor_capture_mapping_v1.xlsx) — it includes suggested HubSpot property targets and example payload rows. Can you share a sample CSV or the field list you want captured?

Techops questions:
- Do your scanners include badge ID and a capture timestamp?
- What is the expected volume per hour (peak)?

Next steps: if you confirm a sample payload, Marissa (cc'd) will draft compliant consent language and Ben will propose a short MAP for milestone tracking. If it works for you, we can do a 30-min tech run Friday (calendar TBD).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding the privacy/consent guidance you requested. Below is a short, field-ready consent snippet we recommend for the scanner/form UI. Please confirm if you need regional language tweaks for GDPR.

Consent (short):
"I agree to be contacted by EventWorks and its partners for event-related follow-ups. I understand my data will be processed for sales and marketing purposes and may be stored for up to 24 months. I may opt out at any time."

Required metadata to capture: consent_given (true/false), consent_ts (ISO8601), consent_method (scanner/form), consent_text_version.

EU-specific addition (if applicable): "By providing your details you consent to processing under our legitimate interest and may request erasure or restriction at any time."

I've attached a text file with the copy variants (sample_consent_text.txt). Once we agree on language, Laura will sign off and Ben will note it in the MAP.
